agora.title: Agora — Debate graph
agora.description: An exploration of how to make public disagreements easier to understand by connecting arguments, objections, responses, facts and sources without imposing a conclusion.
agora.why: Public debate often mixes facts, interpretations, causal claims, predictions and values. Agora aims to make these differences visible so that people can better understand where a disagreement actually lies.
agora.objective: Organize a public question as a graph of supporting and opposing arguments, objections, responses, evidence and sources. The goal is not to tell people what to think, but to make reasoning easier to examine and challenge.
agora.design: Present the strongest arguments from different positions, preserve original sources, make uncertainty visible and avoid simplistic truth scores when a controversy also involves values.
agora.status: An unpublished local prototype already makes it possible to explore a demonstration debate through a graph and an accessible text view, search and filter its elements, consult their sources and prepare a contribution that remains in the browser. It does not yet include accounts, remote collaboration or a public moderation system.
agora.questions: The initial audience, editorial governance, contribution verification, moderation, hosting and future connections with Reflection Studio and the Democratic Observatory remain to be defined.

about.bio:
As a software developer and IT analyst at PREPAR-VIE, I work on business applications in the life insurance sector. My background combines computing and finance, requirements analysis, development and an understanding of operational constraints.

What engages me extends far beyond this field: human and collective questions, behaviour, the quality of public debate and democratic participation. My thinking draws on psychology, sociology, philosophy and geopolitics, alongside questions of freedom, responsibility, and individual and digital sovereignty.

I value in-depth discussion, serious engagement with opposing arguments and pluralism. Technology is also an object of critical reflection: I am as interested in its possibilities as in the dependencies, power structures and forms of surveillance it can create.

I want to contribute to demanding, meaningful projects, digital or otherwise. My writing and travels belong here too: they are part of what I learn, what I question and how my perspective develops.
